builder_plan.scenario: A workflow needs specialist review, but extra agents may add more cost than useful work.
builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Teamknitt: Configuring, Observing and Intervening in LLM-Agent Teams through the Lens of Dynamical-Systems and Human-Team Theory
summary: Teamknitt replaces ad hoc, hard-coded multi-agent wiring (fixed routing, uncontrolled context passing, no mid-run human control) with explicit configuration of routing topologies, sharing profiles, and dependency-boundary interventions, plus structured observability views. It costs engineering complexity: configuring up to 16 agents, fourteen topologies or custom graphs, and human-led review cycles adds orchestration overhead and multiplies API token spend relative to a single-agent loop. It can fail because the paper reports no comparative results, so the hypothesized links between topology, information flow, fractal communication scaling, and performance are unvalidated, and emergent states such as trust are explicitly unmeasured, leaving teams to tune topology blind.
rationale: The framework is implementable on constrained infrastructure via third-party APIs, but with zero empirical results every benefit is a falsifiable hypothesis, so small-scale workload-specific validation is required before any production adoption.
technique: Theory-driven multi-agent team configuration and intervention framework
